title: Sustainable fabrics of the future
titleChinese: 既环保又耐用的未来服装面料
paragraphs: Choosing what to wear can be a tricky problem, especially if you’re a fashion victim. Trying to keep up with the latest styles involves regular visits to the shops and sometimes forking out for expensive designer clothes. But when the fashion changes, these clothes languish in the back of cupboards gathering dust, or just get thrown away.

There are many stores that now offer cheap ‘fast fashion’ – low-price items that imitate the styles of more expensive designer brands. Environmentalists are angered by the amount of energy involved in making these clothes and that many of them are made from non-recyclable materials. This means that items are just incinerated or go into landfill.

Writing about this for the BBC, Eleanor Lawrie says that people in the UK are the worst in Europe for doing this - with a million tonnes of unwanted textiles a year being discarded. And she says “on top of often poor labour conditions for garment workers, the fashion industry is responsible for 20% of the world's waste water, and 10% of carbon emissions.”

This is something the fashion industry is becoming more aware of and has led to a new crop of biomaterials that replace wasteful textiles like cotton and leather. Examples include Piñatex, a leather-like substance made from discarded pineapple leaves. It's been used in collections by Hugo Boss and H&M. And there’s mycelium, the root structure of mushrooms, that’s being used to create food, packaging and textiles.

Cotton is a very resource-intense crop to grow. Eleanor Lawrie says “about 15,000 litres of water [are] required to make one pair of jeans.” So, buying organic cotton is a better choice. And there is also Tencel, also known as Lyocell, a natural product that's now growing in popularity. It's made by extracting cellulose fibre from trees; its manufacture is thought to use 95% less water than cotton processing.

But creating sustainable textiles is only part of the battle – buying ethically, buying second hand and buying fewer clothes are the obvious environmentally friendly choices. Dr Richard Blackburn from Leeds School of Design told the BBC that “I don't think you should consider buying any item of clothing unless you commit to 30 wears. Unless you can do that you're not even starting to be sustainable.”

vocabulary.entry: tricky /ˈtrɪki/ adj. 棘手的；难处理的
vocabulary.example: This is a tricky problem that requires careful consideration.
vocabulary.translation: 这是一个需要仔细考虑的棘手问题。

vocabulary.entry: fashion victim /ˈfæʃn ˈvɪktɪm/ 时尚受害者（指盲目追求潮流、被时尚左右的人）
vocabulary.example: She's such a fashion victim that she buys new clothes every week.
vocabulary.translation: 她真是个时尚受害者，每周都买新衣服。

vocabulary.entry: keep up with /kiːp ʌp wɪð/ 跟上；不落后于
vocabulary.example: It's hard to keep up with the latest technology.
vocabulary.translation: 跟上最新的技术发展很难。

vocabulary.entry: fork out /fɔːk aʊt/ 花大价钱；支付
vocabulary.example: I had to fork out a lot of money for the car repairs.
vocabulary.translation: 我不得不花一大笔钱修车。

vocabulary.entry: designer clothes /dɪˈzaɪnə kləʊðz/ 设计师品牌服装
vocabulary.example: She only wears designer clothes to important events.
vocabulary.translation: 她只在重要场合穿设计师品牌服装。

vocabulary.entry: languish /ˈlæŋɡwɪʃ/ v. 被闲置；被冷落
vocabulary.example: The old furniture has been languishing in the attic for years.
vocabulary.translation: 这些旧家具已经在阁楼里闲置多年了。

vocabulary.entry: fast fashion /ˌfɑːst ˈfæʃn/ 快时尚
vocabulary.example: Fast fashion brands produce cheap, trendy clothes quickly.
vocabulary.translation: 快时尚品牌快速生产廉价、时髦的服装。

vocabulary.entry: imitate /ˈɪmɪteɪt/ v. 模仿；仿效
vocabulary.example: The artist imitated the style of Van Gogh in his paintings.
vocabulary.translation: 这位艺术家在画作中模仿了梵高的风格。

vocabulary.entry: non-recyclable /ˌnɒn rɪˈsaɪkləbl/ adj. 不可回收的
vocabulary.example: These plastic bags are non-recyclable and harm the environment.
vocabulary.translation: 这些塑料袋不可回收，对环境有害。

vocabulary.entry: incinerate /ɪnˈsɪnəreɪt/ v. 焚烧；火化
vocabulary.example: The waste is incinerated to reduce its volume.
vocabulary.translation: 垃圾被焚烧以减少体积。

vocabulary.entry: textile /ˈtekstaɪl/ n. 纺织品；织物
vocabulary.example: The factory produces textiles for clothing and home furnishings.
vocabulary.translation: 这家工厂生产用于服装和家居装饰的纺织品。

vocabulary.entry: discard /dɪˈskɑːd/ v. 丢弃；抛弃
vocabulary.example: She discarded the old magazines that were taking up space.
vocabulary.translation: 她扔掉了占地方的旧杂志。

vocabulary.entry: garment worker /ˈɡɑːmənt ˈwɜːkə(r)/ 服装工人
vocabulary.example: Garment workers in some countries are paid very low wages.
vocabulary.translation: 一些国家的服装工人工资很低。

vocabulary.entry: biomaterial /ˌbaɪəʊməˈtɪəriəl/ n. 生物材料
vocabulary.example: Scientists are developing new biomaterials for medical use.
vocabulary.translation: 科学家们正在开发用于医疗的新型生物材料。

vocabulary.entry: extract /ɪkˈstrækt/ v. 提取；提炼
vocabulary.example: Oil is extracted from olives to make olive oil.
vocabulary.translation: 从橄榄中提取油脂制作橄榄油。

vocabulary.entry: cellulose fibre /ˈseljʊləʊs ˈfaɪbə(r)/ 纤维素纤维
vocabulary.example: Cellulose fibre is a key component of plant cell walls.
vocabulary.translation: 纤维素纤维是植物细胞壁的关键成分。

vocabulary.entry: sustainable /səˈsteɪnəbl/ adj. 可持续的；不破坏环境的
vocabulary.example: We need to find sustainable solutions to energy problems.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要找到解决能源问题的可持续方案。

vocabulary.entry: ethical /ˈeθɪkl/ adj. 道德的；合乎道德的
vocabulary.example: The company is committed to ethical business practices.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司致力于道德经营。

vocabulary.entry: second hand /ˌsekənd ˈhænd/ adj. 二手的；旧的
vocabulary.example: She bought a second hand car to save money.
vocabulary.translation: 她为了省钱买了一辆二手车。

vocabulary.entry: resource-intense /rɪˈsɔːs ɪnˈtens/ adj. 耗资源的；资源密集型的
vocabulary.example: Mining is a resource-intense industry.
vocabulary.translation: 采矿是一个资源密集型产业。

vocabulary.entry: organic cotton /ɔːˈɡænɪk ˈkɒtn/ 有机棉
vocabulary.example: Organic cotton is grown without harmful pesticides.
vocabulary.translation: 有机棉的种植不使用有害农药。

vocabulary.entry: commit to /kəˈmɪt tu/ 承诺；保证
vocabulary.example: She committed to finishing the project by the end of the month.
vocabulary.translation: 她承诺在月底前完成这个项目。

sentences.english: Choosing what to wear can be a tricky problem, especially if you’re a fashion victim.
sentences.chinese: 选衣服有时候是个棘手的问题，尤其如果你是一个“时尚受害者”的话。

sentences.english: Trying to keep up with the latest styles involves regular visits to the shops and sometimes forking out for expensive designer clothes.
sentences.chinese: 想要跟上最新潮流，就得经常逛商店，有时还得花大价钱买昂贵的设计师品牌服装。

sentences.english: But when the fashion changes, these clothes languish in the back of cupboards gathering dust, or just get thrown away.
sentences.chinese: 但当潮流改变时，这些衣服就会被闲置在衣柜深处积灰，或者干脆被扔掉。

sentences.english: There are many stores that now offer cheap ‘fast fashion’ – low-price items that imitate the styles of more expensive designer brands.
sentences.chinese: 现在有很多商店都在售卖廉价的“快时尚”产品——这些低价商品模仿高价设计师品牌的款式。

sentences.english: Environmentalists are angered by the amount of energy involved in making these clothes and that many of them are made from non-recyclable materials.
sentences.chinese: 环保人士对生产这些衣服所耗费的大量能源感到愤怒，而且其中许多衣服是由不可回收材料制成的。

sentences.english: This means that items are just incinerated or go into landfill.
sentences.chinese: 这意味着这些衣物最终只会被焚烧或送进垃圾填埋场。

sentences.english: Writing about this for the BBC, Eleanor Lawrie says that people in the UK are the worst in Europe for doing this - with a million tonnes of unwanted textiles a year being discarded.
sentences.chinese: 埃莉诺·劳里在为英国广播公司撰写相关文章时表示，英国人在这方面是欧洲最糟糕的——每年有100万吨废弃纺织品被丢弃。

sentences.english: And she says “on top of often poor labour conditions for garment workers, the fashion industry is responsible for 20% of the world's waste water, and 10% of carbon emissions.”
sentences.chinese: 她还说：“除了服装工人往往面临恶劣的劳动条件外，时尚产业还造成了全球20%的废水排放和10%的碳排放。”

sentences.english: This is something the fashion industry is becoming more aware of and has led to a new crop of biomaterials that replace wasteful textiles like cotton and leather.
sentences.chinese: 时尚产业逐渐意识到这一问题，这也催生了一批新型生物材料，以替代棉花和皮革等耗资源的纺织品。

sentences.english: Examples include Piñatex, a leather-like substance made from discarded pineapple leaves. It's been used in collections by Hugo Boss and H&M.
sentences.chinese: 例如，Piñatex（菠萝皮皮革）是一种由废弃菠萝叶制成的类皮革材料，已被雨果博斯（Hugo Boss）和H&M用于服装系列中。

sentences.english: And there’s mycelium, the root structure of mushrooms, that’s being used to create food, packaging and textiles.
sentences.chinese: 还有菌丝体（蘑菇的根系结构），目前正被用于生产食品、包装和纺织品。

sentences.english: Cotton is a very resource-intense crop to grow.
sentences.chinese: 棉花是一种种植过程消耗资源极高的作物。

sentences.english: Eleanor Lawrie says “about 15,000 litres of water [are] required to make one pair of jeans.”
sentences.chinese: 埃莉诺·劳里说：“制作一条牛仔裤大约需要15000升水。”

sentences.english: So, buying organic cotton is a better choice.
sentences.chinese: 因此，购买有机棉是更好的选择。

sentences.english: And there is also Tencel, also known as Lyocell, a natural product that's now growing in popularity.
sentences.chinese: 此外还有天丝（Tencel，也称为莱赛尔纤维），这是一种天然产品，如今正越来越受欢迎。

sentences.english: It's made by extracting cellulose fibre from trees; its manufacture is thought to use 95% less water than cotton processing.
sentences.chinese: 它通过从树木中提取纤维素纤维制成，其生产过程消耗的水量据信比棉花加工少95%。

sentences.english: But creating sustainable textiles is only part of the battle – buying ethically, buying second hand and buying fewer clothes are the obvious environmentally friendly choices.
sentences.chinese: 但制造可持续纺织品只是这场战役的一部分——理性消费（关注环保及劳工权益）、购买二手衣物以及减少购衣数量，才是显而易见的环保选择。

sentences.english: Dr Richard Blackburn from Leeds School of Design told the BBC that “I don't think you should consider buying any item of clothing unless you commit to 30 wears.
sentences.chinese: 利兹设计学院的理查德·布莱克本博士向英国广播公司表示：“我认为，除非你能保证一件衣服穿30次以上，否则就不应该考虑购买它。

sentences.english: Unless you can do that you're not even starting to be sustainable.”
sentences.chinese: 如果做不到这一点，你就根本算不上开始践行可持续理念。”
